statement:
Find the complete set of values of $p$ for which the equation
$$x^2-2px+y^2-6y-p^2+8p+9=0$$
describes a circle in the $x$-$y$ plane.
solution:
Complete the square for $x$ and $y$:
$$(x-p)^2-p^2+(y-3)^2-9-p^2+8p+9=0,$$
which simplifies to
$$(x-p)^2+(y-3)^2=2p^2-8p.$$

This is a circle (with centre $(p,3)$) exactly when the squared radius $2p^2-8p$ is positive:
$$2p^2-8p>0 \quad\Rightarrow\quad p(p-4)>0.$$

The quadratic $p(p-4)$ has roots $0$ and $4$ and is positive outside the roots, so
$$p<0\ \text{or}\ p>4,$$
which is **option D**.
hints: Complete the square to put the equation in circle form.
The squared radius must be positive.
Solve the quadratic inequality in p.
